> **Variant Perception:** The Street is pricing NVO at a trailing P/E of **10.9x**[1] and **EV/EBITDA of 7.6x**[1] — multiples that embed a permanent-impairment scenario for US GLP-1 pricing. ## SECTION 2 — STRUCTURAL ECONOMICS NARRATIVE

### The GLP-1 Duopoly Captures >90% of Profit Pools, But the Margin at the Top Is Compressing

Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly together command approximately **90% of global GLP-1 revenue**[4], operating as a differentiated duopoly in which competition is waged on efficacy and formulation rather than price — until now. The value chain concentrates gross margin at the API manufacturing and drug-product formulation steps (**~70–80% and ~75–85% respectively**)[5], with commodity-level returns at distribution (**3–6%**)[5] and PBM-captured rebates (**20–30%**)[5] representing leakage below the originator level. Novo's full vertical integration across R&D, API synthesis, fill-finish, and commercialisation means it retains the full originator margin stack — a structural advantage that manifests in the company's FY2025 gross margin of **81.0%**[6] [as of training cutoff].

### Lilly's Tirzepatide Is a Structural Format Shift, Not a Price War — Duration Matters

This is not a cyclical price war. Eli Lilly's tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) achieves **~25.5% body weight reduction**[7] vs. semaglutide's **~15–17%**[7] in comparable trials — a product-performance gap that, absent a Novo counter-innovation, is durable and will continue to shift prescriber preference. Novo's volume share has declined from **~70% in 2023 to 59.6% in FY2025**[8], confirming that this is a **structural Format Shift** driven by therapeutic superiority, not a temporary pricing promotion. The valuation implication is that any multiple assigned to Novo's current obesity franchise must discount the possibility of further share erosion unless Amycretin (Phase 3 starting Q1 2026)[9] or a next-generation molecule closes the efficacy gap.

Novo is attempting to rebuild switching costs through convenience differentiation. The oral semaglutide tablet deploys SNAC (sodium N-[8-(2-hydroxybenzoyl) amino] caprylate) carrier technology that is **separately patent-protected beyond the 2031 compound patent**[3], creating a formulation-specific moat that biosimilar manufacturers cannot immediately replicate. If the 12-month persistence rate for oral patients matches or exceeds the injectable cohort, this represents a structural TRx floor that the Street is not yet pricing.

FY2025 capital expenditure reached **DKK 90.1 billion**[1] — a **76% YoY increase** from DKK 51.3 billion in FY2024[1] and representing **~29% of FY2025 revenue**[1] (vs. a 5-year average of approximately 15%). **2A.5 Profit Pool Shift**

The margin layer is now moving from injectable GLP-1 to oral formulations, which carry lower COGS per patient but higher adherence (and thus higher LTV).

Novo Nordisk owns this toll booth through its DKK 100B+ invested in proprietary API and drug-product manufacturing capacity [2]. **2B.1 Market Structure Classification: Duopoly**

The branded GLP-1 obesity and diabetes market is a **duopoly** between Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly. Together they command ~90% of global GLP-1 revenue [17]. **2B.3 Basis of Competition — Customer Purchase Decision Ranking**

2. **Regulatory compliance / FDA approval** (indication expansion, e.g., CV outcomes)
3. **Switching cost / ecosystem** (formulary placement, insurer contracts, doctor familiarity)
4. **Payer access / price** (increasingly important post-Medicare negotiation)
5. **Convenience** (oral vs. injectable, weekly vs. daily)
6. **Brand / trust** (secondary in B2B2C pharma)

Novo Nordisk avoids commodity pricing through **formulation innovation** (oral semaglutide) and **indication expansion** (Wegovy approved for CV risk reduction, MASH exploration via Akero acquisition), which allow premium positioning even as list prices decline under government pressure.

**2B.4 Competitive Response Profile**

When Novo Nordisk gains share (e.g., oral Wegovy launch), competitors respond with **product investment** (Lilly's orforglipron oral GLP-1 Phase 3 readout expected 2026) and **M&A** (Lilly's own pipeline additions, Pfizer's $10B Metsera acquisition [19]). Novo does not see price-based retaliation — instead, the competitive arms race is in **next-generation molecules** (tri-agonists, amycretin).

2D. INDUSTRY CYCLE POSITIONING
──────────────────────────────────────────

**2D.1 Industry Lifecycle Stage: Growth → Early Shakeout**

The GLP-1 obesity/diabetes market is transitioning from the **growth** phase into an **early shakeout** phase. Evidence:
- Industry revenue CAGR: The GLP-1 market grew from ~$22B in 2024 to an estimated $70–94B in 2025 [29, 30], representing ~100%+ YoY growth.
- Competitor count: >30 companies have GLP-1 or multi-agonist programs in clinical development [31], but only Novo and Lilly have commercial products at scale.
- M&A acceleration: Pfizer/Metsera ($10B), Novo/Akero ($4.7B), Roche/Carmot, GSK/MASH deals in 2025 alone [19, 8]. This pattern — large pharma buying pre-revenue biotechs to fill pipeline gaps — is characteristic of late-growth/early-shakeout.
- **The shakeout signal:** CagriSema failure (Feb 2026) and multiple competitor trial disappointments are beginning to separate credible programs from speculative ones. Analysts predict 3–5 obesity programs will be abandoned by 2027 [32].

**2D.2 Cyclical vs Structural Demand**

GLP-1 demand is **overwhelmingly structural** (obesity prevalence is secular, not cyclical) but **cyclically elevated** in the near term due to: (i) pent-up demand from years of supply constraints, (ii) Medicare coverage expansion for obesity with comorbidities (beginning April 2026) [33], and (iii) social media-driven awareness.

**Mid-cycle revenue estimate:** Based on current growth deceleration (from 50%+ YoY in 2023 to 10% in 2025 [13]), the market is normalising. Novo's FY2025 revenue of $309.1B [12] includes a ~15–20% cyclical premium from supply-constrained pricing power. A mid-cycle revenue estimate for Novo would be ~$260–275B, assuming normalised growth rates of 8–12% in the GLP-1 class.

**Cycle position: Late-cycle within the growth phase.** Growth rates are decelerating, pricing is under pressure, and competitive intensity is rising.

**2D.3 Capacity and Supply Dynamics**

- **Current utilisation:** Novo Nordisk's manufacturing facilities were operating at or near full utilisation through 2024–2025, with Ozempic and Wegovy on the FDA drug shortage list for much of 2024 [34].
- **New capacity announced:** DKK 60B capex in 2025, DKK 55B in 2026 [35]. Ireland facility expansion (€432M) announced March 2026 [16]. Kalundborg, Denmark API expansion underway [36].
- **Time to bring online:** New peptide manufacturing facilities take 3–4 years from groundbreaking to GMP production. Novo's 2023–2025 investments should begin contributing to volume by 2027–2029.
- **Pricing power emergence threshold:** When utilisation falls below ~85%, pricing power erodes. Novo is currently building capacity ahead of demand, suggesting pricing pressure will persist through 2027.

**2D.4 Inventory Cycle (Applicable to Drug Product)**

Not directly applicable in the traditional sense — pharmaceutical inventory is regulated (FDA track-and-trace). However, channel inventory at wholesalers has been destocking through H2 2025 as Novo rebuilt supply. Typical pharma channel inventory is 30–45 days; Novo's has been normalising after the 2023–2024 shortage period [34].

Obesity care revenue as a % of total sales is the best predictor of EBITDA margin 12 months forward:
- Obesity care has higher gross margins than diabetes care (premium pricing, lower COGS per patient at scale)
- FY2025: Obesity care sales were DKK 82.3 billion (31% CER growth) [15], representing ~35–36% of total sales
- As obesity care mix rises, blended EBITDA margin should expand — **but this is being offset by US pricing pressure**
- **Key offset:** US Medicare pricing (71% discount) [26] and the $4.2B reversal of 340B rebate provisions in 2026 guidance [45] will compress margins despite favorable mix

**2F.4 The Risk Indicator: Win Rate vs. Eli Lilly (Head-to-Head Prescriber Preference)**

The early warning signal for competitive deterioration is **prescriber preference in head-to-head settings**:
- **Current reading:** CagriSema failed to beat tirzepatide in a head-to-head Phase 3 trial (23.0% vs. 25.5% weight loss) [6], which triggered at least 7 analyst downgrades [46]
- Wegovy pill is outperforming Lilly's oral candidate orforglipron in indirect comparison (greater weight loss, lower discontinuation) [47]
- **Threshold for re-evaluation:** If Lilly's oral GLP-1 (orforglipron) shows superior efficacy to oral semaglutide in a direct comparison trial, or if Lilly achieves >50% value market share in the US (currently ~50%+ per some estimates [15]), the competitive position would materially deteriorate.

2. **FDA Drug Shortages List** — tracks supply constraints for Ozempic/Wegovy; indicates capacity utilisation [34].

**2F.6 Management Guidance & Forward Estimates**

From Novo Nordisk's Q4 2025 / Full Year 2025 earnings release and investor presentation (February 3–5, 2026):

- **FY2026 Adjusted Sales Guidance (at CER):** −5% to −13% [14]

**One-time items excluded from 2026 guidance:**
- $4.2 billion reversal of 340B rebate provisions [45] — this is a significant accounting adjustment that inflates the "as reported" vs. "adjusted" gap

**FY2027 Guidance:** No quantitative FY2027 guidance has been provided as of the Q4 2025 earnings call. Management referenced amycretin Phase 3 initiation in Q1 2026 [37] and a potential CagriSema reformulation study [48], but did not provide revenue or EBITDA targets for FY2027.

• The dominant theme is Novo Nordisk's multi-wave obesity pipeline — Amycretin Phase 3 and oral Wegovy represent the next growth legs beyond semaglutide, with a 58% probability of closing the efficacy gap against Lilly's tirzepatide.
